newsitem.title: GERMANY: VEW's Harpen expects higher 96 net profit.
newsitem.headline: VEW's Harpen expects higher 96 net profit.

text.p: Harpen AG, the services unit of the German utility group VEW AG said on Monday that it expected to report an increase in net profit in 1996, despite a slack German residential property market.

"We have no empty units and with a zero percent rate we are probably leaders among real estate companies," Rolf Bierwirth, management board chairman of Harpen, said. Harpen is also active in the transport, energy and environmental sectors.
The group said it expected sales to increase to 300 million marks in 1996, up from 218 million marks last time, and for net profit to rise from 1995's figure of 33 million marks.
Harpen's parent, VEW, said in November that it too expected a moderate rise in net profits in full-year 1996.
